$comment: CRITICAL INTERACTION CONTRACT MANIFEST (B1857905, reliability programme R2).
Maps a stable contract id (never renamed by a line-number shift or a comment edit — see
R1's 'identity based on source line numbers' caution in docs/RELIABILITY-PROGRAMME.md) to the
existing e2e spec file that proves it. playwright.critical.config.js reads this file to decide
which specs to run; scripts/lib/e2eDrift.mjs's checkRequiredContracts() reads it to decide
whether every contract's cases ran and ALL PASSED — no failure, no skip, no flaky retry-pass
counts as proof (spec.ok alone was never enough evidence; see R1's collectCases fix).
DELIBERATELY SMALL TO START, per R2's own 'begin small, expand by risk' instruction: two
contracts, both already-existing REAL specs reused as-is (never duplicated), neither needing
the seeded test account, so this lane runs identically whether or not
E2E_EMAIL/E2E_PASSWORD are configured (proven: e2e/auth.setup.js's own case skips cleanly and
is not part of either contract).
PROVEN RELIABLE BEFORE WIRING (2026-09-27): 8 consecutive full runs against a real local
build/preview in this sandbox, 0 flakes, 0 unexplained failures.
⛔ R3 (B1857905) REPAIRED THE TWO CASES R2 HAD TO EXCLUDE — both are back in their file's
required contract, no grepInvert left in playwright.critical.config.js. What was stale and
what changed, briefly (full account on each spec's own R3 comment):
- 'a refused Delete explains where the keystroke went' (inspector-key-scope.spec.js) — the
setup used to leave the Depth field via Enter, which keeps focus ON the field (SCOPE.FIELD)
and NEW-1/B754752 deliberately made a FIELD refusal silent (no toast, on purpose — see
lib/keyContract.js's shouldHintRefusal). Repaired to leave via Tab onto the field's own
stepper button instead, landing on SCOPE.CHROME, which still hints — proving the SAME
safety property (Delete never reaches the plan from inside the field) with a setup the
current product still narrates.
- 'drag the Fill-opacity slider, then Ctrl+Z WITHOUT deselecting still undoes it'
(ctrlz-undo.spec.js) — a building's Fill opacity is no longer `input[type="range"]` (it is
PercentField/NumInput now, a plain text field — deliberately, part of the dimension-field
rework). Repaired to draw a markup CLOUD shape instead: its Fill opacity is still a literal
range slider (the one closed-markup kind that is not `simpleClosedMarkup`), so the test now
exercises the one remaining SCOPE.SLIDER instance of the exact contract it was written to
prove, rather than a FIELD-scoped contract the product no longer has for a building.
Both repairs mutation-proven red-on-regression / green-on-correct before being restored.
Adding a contract here is a deliberate act, same spirit as known-red.json's --allow-grow
--item: name the id, the file, and the backlog item that owns expanding this lane. Removing
one narrows required coverage and should be rare and explained on its item.

contracts.why: Ctrl+Z must peel one vertex mid-draw (Bluebeam parity) and never silently revert a committed shape or the wrong one; owner-reported.
a keystroke typed into an inspector field must never delete the plan; owner-reported and reproduced on his real rows (FM 359 / Concept A).
